title: Structured Troubleshooting
summary: Advance from likely causes to safe tests, observations, documentation, and escalation.
objectives: Apply a structured troubleshooting sequence to a simulated issue.
Choose a safe test and document its result before escalating.

vocab.def: A possible explanation that can be checked against evidence.
Ask a more qualified person or team to take over or advise.
An approved check that gathers information without creating unnecessary risk.

sections.heading: Use a repeatable method
sections.body: Define the problem, gather evidence, identify the affected system, form possible causes, test the safest simple explanation, observe the result, document it, and escalate when needed.

sections.heading: Scenarios need different evidence
sections.body: A service that cannot connect may need path evidence. Storage nearly full may need capacity data. A temperature warning may need trend and airflow context. Do not assume one cause from one symptom.

sections.heading: Stop when the boundary is reached
sections.body: A safe test may be reading an approved status file or comparing a simulated path. Stop before opening hardware, changing production configuration, touching electrical equipment, or accessing unauthorized systems.

practice.prompt: For a simulated storage warning, state the problem, one hypothesis, one safe test, the evidence you would record, and when you would escalate.

quiz.question: What should happen after a safe test?

lab.objective: Work through a synthetic fault using evidence, safe tests, documentation, and escalation.

reflectionPrompt: Which step keeps troubleshooting from becoming random experimentation?
